draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kottayam! It was India's first 100% literate city, and with more than a dozen publishing houses and newspapers based here, people call it the Letter Capital of Kerala. Out here among the rubber trees near Lakkattoor, even the village name comes from jackfruit.
draft.hungryLine: Stick to Kerala food in Kottayam, it's good and everywhere, and the bakeries for fresh bread and snacks are worth a stop.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Wander into Lakkattoor, then on to Mattakkara, the biggest kara in the district. In town, the Thirunakkara Mahadeva Temple has murals from the epics.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Head to Nalumanikkattu Paddy Fields on the Manarcaud to Ettumanoor road for green views and local food.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The Thazhathangady Juma Masjid on the Meenachil river is more than 1,000 years old and is also called the Taj Juma Masjid.

legends.title: The jackfruit village
legends.body: It's believed the name Lakkattoor changed from Plakkattoor, because the area is full of jackfruit trees. Jackfruit is called plakka here.

legends.title: Panchali's bathing pool
legends.body: Local folklore says a pool in these hills was a bathing place for Panchali, the heroine of the Mahabharata. The name of the valley means the place where leaves do not fall.

tips.title: Say if you don't eat beef.
tips.body: Beef is a staple in Kottayam, and a meat roll will very likely have beef in it.

tips.title: Come for the boat races.
tips.body: Around 50 types of traditional boats race in July, August and September during Onam.

story.title: A royal Shiva temple
story.body: The Raja of Thekkumkur built the Thirunakkara Mahadeva Temple at the start of the 16th century. Its walls inside carry murals from the Hindu epics.

story.title: The Little Church
story.body: The same Raja of Thekkumkur built St. Mary's Cheria Palli for his Christian subjects. Its murals of Bible stories were painted with vegetable dyes.

story.title: Ullatt karthas
story.body: Under old Travancore rule, the Mattakkara area was the domain of the Ullatt karthas. Today the area has about 90% literacy.

story.title: Bells from Germany
story.body: Three bells were brought from Germany for St. Mary's Forane Church at Kuravilangad. The church already had a granite cross from around 1597, cut from a single 48 foot block.

story.title: The Letter Capital
story.body: Kottayam is home to over a dozen publishing houses and newspapers, several famous colleges and a university. Grab a paper and see for yourself.
